prompts.title: Form: Recent Rhythm
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 composition. Editorial variant first: kinetic typography on GoatLab charcoal #101412 with warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf. Spanish heading 'FORMA RECIENTE' enters as three stacked letter blocks; team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal' slide from opposite edges. Wins throb in lime, draws lock into slate, losses snap as warm-white outlined type. Use a rhythmic three-beat cadence, a quick lateral whip-pan and a settle into a single focal typographic lockup. No statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events; lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow subtitles. Transition: the lockup collapses into a thin lime rule. Statistical variant: same 9:16 frame, two clustered groups of count bars for wins, draws and losses, shared zero baseline, equal bar width and Spanish labels 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas'; unit 'partidos'. Value tags bind to {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}, {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Sample annotation must show {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} so unequal samples are explicit; if equal, both are still labeled. Small slate source/sample line from the catalog sits under the chart. Layout: title top eighth, chart upper three-fifths, legend row at mid, source/sample at baseline; condensed sans headings, tabular numerals, Spanish labels in sentence case. Entry: baseline draws in, bars grow upward in staggered order, tags fade. Main comparison: home cluster vs away cluster; emphasis on the tallest win bar with lime glow, then a slate underline under the draw column. Camera: slow push-in from half-height to center, no rotation. Transition: bars flatten to baseline and swipe away; exit holds source/sample for two beats before clean cut.

prompts.title: Goals: For and Against
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Editorial first: illustrative football pitch in charcoal #101412 with thin warm-white markings, lime ball trail and slate shadow; Spanish heading 'GOLES' and subheads 'A FAVOR' and 'EN CONTRA'. The ball traces an abstract arc from centre to two glowing zones, one lime and one slate, while team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal' reveal as clean type cards. Motion is fluid and rhythmic: pitch lines draw on, ball path whips through, type cards punch in; no statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles. Transition: ball trail stretches into a horizontal lime line. Statistical variant: paired horizontal bars for both teams, two bars per team for goals for and goals against, common scale across all bars, shared zero baseline, Spanish labels 'Goles a favor', 'Goles en contra', team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal', unit 'goles'. Values bind to {{home.gf}}, {{home.ga}}, {{away.gf}}, {{away.ga}}. Sample annotation shows {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} from the catalog; source/sample line in small slate type below chart. Layout: title top, two team rows at center, value tags right-aligned, legend with lime for for and slate for against. Entry: axis and zero line draw, bars grow from zero in paired sequence, labels fade. Main comparison: Liverpool's for/against pair against Villarreal's pair; emphasis on the largest contrast with a lime outline, not a prediction. Camera: slow vertical drift upward, then lock. Transition: bars compress into a single line and wipe; exit leaves source/sample visible for two beats.

prompts.title: Clean Sheets: Defensive Shield
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Editorial first: defensive energy as a stylised shield built from charcoal #101412 plates, warm-white edge light, lime pulse and slate shadow. Spanish heading 'ARCOS EN CERO' with team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal' on two shield halves. Shields snap together, ripple with a low defensive pulse, then separate into a single focal beat; kinetic type 'SOLIDEZ' flashes briefly. No statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow subtitles. Transition: shield edge becomes a thin horizontal rule. Statistical variant: two clean-sheet count columns, one per team, shared zero baseline, equal width, Spanish labels 'Arcos en cero' and 'Partidos en la muestra'; unit 'partidos'. Values bind to {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}; sample annotation must display {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} beside each column so counts stay counts. Do not convert counts into rates. Source/sample line in slate under chart. Layout: title top, two columns upper center, value tags above each column, sample labels below; condensed sans headings, tabular numerals, Spanish labels in sentence case. Entry: baseline draws, columns rise, shield motif dissolves into column caps. Main comparison: Liverpool column vs Villarreal column; emphasis on the taller count with lime cap and a warm-white ring, while the shorter count stays slate. Camera: slow push-in, no rotation. Transition: columns flatten and slide into next scene; exit holds source/sample for two beats.

prompts.title: Head-to-Head: Historical Duel
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Editorial first: a visual duel, two vertical team monoliths in charcoal #101412 facing across a warm-white centre line, lime energy on the Liverpool side and slate energy on the Villarreal side. Spanish heading 'CRUCES PREVIOS' and team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal' appear as opposing type columns; quick lateral camera whip creates duel tension, then locks into a single focal centre mark. No statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles. Transition: centre line flashes lime and cuts to chart. Statistical variant: horizontal count bars for historical wins and draws, shared zero baseline, Spanish labels 'Victorias Liverpool', 'Empates', 'Victorias Villarreal', 'Cruces previos'; unit 'partidos'. Values bind to {{h2h.homeWins}}, {{h2h.draws}}, {{h2h.awayWins}}; total sample annotated as {{h2h.total}}. Source/sample line in slate below chart. Layout: title top, bars in three rows, value tags right, total sample badge near title; warm-white type, lime home edge, slate away edge. Entry: zero line draws, bars grow horizontally, total badge fades. Main comparison: home wins vs away wins with draw row held between; emphasis on the larger win count with lime edge, draw row in slate. Add Spanish note 'Datos históricos, no pronóstico'. Camera: slow lateral drift then settle. Transition: bars retract to zero and centre line returns; exit holds source/sample for two beats.

prompts.title: Synthesis: Attack vs Solidity
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Editorial first: team reveals with narrative emphasis. Charcoal #101412 stage, warm-white type, lime for Liverpool and slate for Villarreal. Spanish heading 'CONTRASTE' and subheads 'ATAQUE' and 'SOLIDEZ'; team name cards reveal in sequence, then a split-screen tension: lime attack ribbon pushes from left, slate defensive wall slides from right, meeting at a warm-white seam. No statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Lower quarter clear for permanent yellow subtitles. Transition: seam becomes a thin rule. Statistical variant: two side-by-side mini-panels on a common goal scale, shared zero baseline, Spanish labels 'Goles a favor' and 'Goles en contra', team names 'Liverpool' and 'Villarreal', unit 'goles'. Left panel compares {{home.gf}} and {{away.gf}}; right panel compares {{home.ga}} and {{away.ga}}. Do not combine into an index or forecast. Source/sample line cites the catalog source and attached sample for each fact; no model estimate is shown because none is supplied. Add Spanish note 'Historial, no estimación'. Layout: title top, two panels upper three-fifths, value tags aligned, source/sample below; condensed sans headings, tabular numerals. Entry: both panels draw baselines, bars rise in paired sequence, seam motif dissolves into panel divider. Main comparison: attacking output in left panel vs defensive concession in right panel; emphasis alternates once between lime and slate without declaring a winner. Camera: slow push-in, then micro-pullback. Transition: panels fold into a single line and wipe; exit holds source/sample for two beats.
